writing_synthetic_unvalidated.essay: Rapid urbanization has triggered acute housing shortages in metropolitan areas worldwide, driving property prices and rents beyond the reach of average earners. writing_synthetic_unvalidated.essay: The root causes of criminality have long been debated among criminologists, psychologists, and legal scholars. While some researchers contend that genetic predispositions play a role in antisocial behavior, I hold the view that environmental influences—such as poverty, education, and family structure—are the primary determinants of criminal activity. Biological arguments suggest that hereditary traits, such as neurological imbalances or impulsive temperaments, may incline certain individuals toward aggressive behavior. However, genetics alone rarely result in crime unless triggered by adverse social conditions. Conversely, social environment exerts a profound and direct influence on individual choices. writing_synthetic_unvalidated.essay: Scientific research forms the cornerstone of technological advancement and societal progress. Private sector funding offers undeniable advantages in speed, capital allocation, and market responsiveness. Pharmaceutical and technology companies invest billions in research and development to bring innovative drugs and consumer products to market rapidly. Driven by competitive pressure, corporate R&D often achieves breakthroughs that transform healthcare and communications. However, private funding suffers from an inherent conflict of interest: corporate research is fundamentally profit-oriented. Private firms rarely invest in non-commercial fields such as basic theoretical physics, environmental conservation, or rare disease treatments. Furthermore, corporate sponsors may suppress findings that undermine their commercial interests. In contrast, government-funded research prioritizes public health, national infrastructure, and long-term scientific exploration without immediate commercial pressure. Publicly funded discoveries—such as the Internet or space technology—are published openly, benefiting humanity as a whole. In conclusion, while private R&D drives commercial products, state-funded scientific research is vital to maintain ethical integrity, open knowledge, and long-term public welfare.

writing_synthetic_unvalidated.essay: The modern university stands at an intersection between vocational training institute and center of intellectual enlightenment. Graduates facing competitive job markets need specialized technical skills, digital literacy, and practical experience to secure immediate employment. In conclusion, higher education should neither be an ivory tower detached from reality nor a trade school servicing corporate needs. writing.essay:
Recently, there have been a lot of discussions about health and whether it is going to 
improve or not. In my opinion, I think that people will become unhealthier in the future than 
they are now. 
There are many reasons that support the idea of people becoming unhealthy in the future. 
Firstly, one reason is that of food. People tend to eat more fast food nowadays. They tend to 
treat themselves with sweets and chocolate whenever they want. This appears to be 
because people are busier now than they used to be. So, people don’t have a chance to 
cook or even learn the art of cookery. Also, having a lot of unhealthy food can lead to obesity 
and it could be a serious issue in the future. Another reason is that technology is developing 
everyday. Young people enjoy buying new gadgets and the latest devices. This has a 
negative impact on their health, especially when they enjoy video games. Spending long 
hours looking at a screen can lead to bad eyesight and obesity as well. Yet another reason 
is that laziness is a big issue. Different forms of exercise might disappear in the future 
because people don’t like sports. Also, people prefer spending most of their time on the 
internet and the internet is growing every single day. 
Other people might disagree and say that health will improve in the future. They believe 
that new sports and new ways to exercise will appear in the future. However, I don’t think it 
can happen since the majority of people spend less time outdoors. Moreover, other people 
believe that technology will try and help people improve their health. For example, there 
have been some games released on the Wii console that makes people exercise but 
technology is developing more in a negative way. For instance, many phone industries are 
developing new applications everyday and today’s generation likes to follow every trend. 
This prevents people to go outside to exercise. They like to spend more time on the internet 
downloading new programmes or reading gossips about celebraties. This affects people’s 
health badly. 
In conclusion, I believe that people’s health is affected negatively by fast food, technology 
and sports and it will be a problem in the future.
writing.band_source: IELTS official sample script — Academic Writing Part 2, Candidate Response 2, awarded Band 7.5 with published examiner comment
writing.examiner_comment:
This is a strong response. A clear position is presented at the outset and some ideas are explored to 
support it. An alternative position is also considered but rejected. Ideas are logically organised and 
there is a clear progression throughout the response. Cohesive devices are generally used flexibly, 
but there is some overuse of sequencers in paragraph 2 [Firstly | So | Also | Yet]. Paragraphing is 
generally effective but could perhaps be used more appropriately by breaking down paragraphs 2 
and 3. 
There is a wide range of vocabulary with good use of less common items as well as evidence of 
higher-level features, such as ‘softening’, e.g. ‘They tend to’, ‘This appears to be’, and ‘might 
disagree’. Errors in spelling and word formation are rare. There is also a variety of complex structures 
with frequent error-free sentences, though some errors do occur and there is some overuse of rather 
short sentence forms.
